newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street seen opening up on benign jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street seen opening up on benign jobs data.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to move higher at the opening on Friday after a benign report on January U.S. employment, dealers said.
Analysts said the actual payroll number came in higher than expected but that the hourly wage component was smaller that forecast, implying that benign inflation continued.
The Labor Department said payrolls grew by 271,000 jobs in January after revised growth of 261,000 in December. A Reuters poll had drawn an average forecast of 237,000 new jobs.
For the market, the beauty of the report was in the details, analysts said.

"The payroll data weren't far enough off the consensus forecast to cause much reaction, so the market focused on the hourly earnings data which is what the Fed is focusing on," said David Sloan, senior economist at I.D.E.A.
Average hourly earnings rose one cent in January, below expectations for a two- or three-cent rise.
Economists said the data suggested reasonably strong economic growth but did not set off any inflation alarms.
